eyas: A young hawk or falcon in the nest, or that has not yet fledged, especially one that will be trained for falconry.
eye: An organ through which animals see (“perceive surroundings via light”).
eyeable: Pleasing to look at; visually appealing; attractive.
eyeballed: Having some specific type of eyeball
eyeballing: present participle and gerund of eyeball
eyebar: A straight bar, usually of metal, with a hole or "eye" at each end to allow it to be fixed to other components.
eyebolt: A bolt with a looped head or an opening in the head.
eyebright: Any of the flowering plants of the genus Euphrasia, originally as used to treat eye infections.
eyebrow: The hair that grows over the bone ridge above the eye socket.
eyedness: The quality of having a dominant eye - one eye that is used more than the other.
eyeful: A full or complete view; a good look.
eyeglass: An artificial lens, especially one of a pair.
eyehole: The hole to which the viewer places his or her eye in a device such as a telescope.
eyehooks: plural of eyehook; alternative form of eye hooks.
eyeing: present participle and gerund of eye
eyelash: One of the hairs which grows along the edge of eyelids.
eyelet: An object that consists of a rim and small hole or perforation to receive a cord or fastener, as in garments, sails, etc.
eyeletting: present participle and gerund of eyelet
eyelid: A thin skin membrane that covers and moves over an eye.
eyeliner: Makeup used to outline the eye, generally applied along or close to the lashline.
eyepiece: The lens (or the component containing a combination of lenses) at the eye end of a microscope or telescope by which the image is viewed.
eyepoint: A point of reference based on the participant's focus, used in generating visual imagery in virtual reality systems.
eyer: One who eyes someone or something.
eyeshade: A type of headgear for shielding the eyes from glaring light, usually consisting of a visor and a headband, more popular among indoor workers in the late-nineteenth and early-tw…
eyeshot: A range of vision, a distance in which something is visible.
eyesight: Vision or the faculty of sight.
eyespot: Any of various primitive light-sensitive organs or regions in many diverse organisms.
eyestalk: A motile stalk having an eye at the tip.
eyestone: A small, lenticular, calcareous body, especially an operculum of a small shell of the family Tubinidae, used to remove a foreign substance from the eye.
eyestrain: Tiredness or pain in the eyes, sometimes accompanied by headache, caused by excessive or improper use of the eyes, or by uncorrected defects of vision.
eyetooth: A canine tooth of the upper jaw in humans.
eyewash: The washing out of the eyes with copious solution (usually water alone) to quickly remove an irritant, as for example in laboratories and industrial plants; the washing solution…
eyewater: A wash or lotion for application to the eyes, such as eyedrops.
eyewear: A vision aid or similar device worn over the eyes, such as eyeglasses, contact lenses, or protective goggles.
eyewitness: Someone who sees an event and can report or testify about it.
eying: present participle and gerund of eye
eyne: Alternative form of eyen: plural of eye.
eyra: A slender, reddish-yellow wild cat (Puma yagouaroundi eyra) ranging from southern Brazil to Texas.
eyre: A journey taken by certain Medieval English itinerant judges (justices in eyre)
eyrie: The nest of a bird of prey.
eyrir: A subdivision of currency, equal to one hundredth of an Icelandic króna
